# Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Nigeria, 2024: initial evidence note

I stopped after a bounded web pass and selected only primary or highly credible sources. The 2024 picture is mixed: macro reform momentum and some institutional support, but also severe cost-of-living pressure, protests, insecurity, and forceful protest policing.

- [Text of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s New Year Address to the Nation](https://statehouse.gov.ng/text-of-president-bola-ahmed-tinubus-new-year-address-to-the-nation/) — State House, January 1, 2024. Claim summary: Tinubu began 2024 by acknowledging high inflation, rising living costs, and the need to revamp the economy and security; this is useful background for the year, not a distinct 2024 event. Question IDs: `8B.*`, `8C.*`

- [IMF Staff Completes 2024 Article IV Mission to Nigeria](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/04/pr2467-nigeria-imf-staff-completes-2024-article-iv-mission) — IMF, March 4, 2024. Claim summary: IMF said the new government inherited a difficult economy marked by low growth, weak revenue, accelerating inflation, and external imbalances; it also flagged food insecurity as an immediate priority and said tighter monetary policy would help curb inflation and naira pressure. Question IDs: `8B.*`, `8D.*`

- [President Tinubu: No Going Back on Reforms; We Remain Steadfast in Creating Investment Opportunities While Tackling Poverty](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-no-going-back-on-reforms-we-remain-steadfast-in-creating-investment-opportunities-while-tackling-poverty/) — State House, February 22, 2024. Claim summary: Tinubu publicly doubled down on his reform agenda and tied it to business growth, investment, and poverty reduction, reinforcing that reform continuity was a central feature of his 2024 posture. Question IDs: `8B.*`, `8D.*`

- [Nigeria: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Statement by the Executive Director for Nigeria](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/05/08/nigeria-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-staff-statement-and-548726) — IMF, May 9, 2024. Claim summary: IMF welcomed the new administration’s “bold reforms,” including fuel subsidy changes, FX-window unification, revenue mobilization, governance measures, and social safety nets, while warning that downside risks remained. Question IDs: `8B.*`, `8D.*`

- [Nigeria: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Statement by the Executive Director for Nigeria](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/102/article-A001-en.xml) — IMF, May 9, 2024. Claim summary: The report’s abstract stressed that years of limited reforms, muted growth, security challenges, and high inflation had already produced food insecurity, poverty, and macro weakness; this is important background for understanding Tinubu’s 2024 term. Question IDs: `8B.*`, `8C.*`, `8D.*`

- [President Tinubu’s Statement on the Killings of Soldiers in Aba](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-statement-on-the-killings-of-soldiers-in-aba/) — State House, June 2, 2024. Claim summary: Tinubu condemned the killing of five soldiers in Aba and vowed a forceful response, showing that insecurity remained an active governing problem in 2024. Question IDs: `8C.*`

- [Turning The Corner: Nigeria’s Ongoing Path of Economic Reforms](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/06/13/turning-the-corner-nigeria-ongoing-path-of-economic-reforms) — World Bank, June 13, 2024. Claim summary: The World Bank said Nigeria was “turning the corner” on macro-fiscal reforms and noted improved FX supply and a smaller official/parallel rate gap, but also said the reforms had intensified cost-of-living pressures and inflation had risen to 33.7 percent in April 2024. Question IDs: `8B.*`, `8D.*`

- [Supporting Nigeria’s Homegrown Reforms: New World Bank Financing for Inclusive Growth and Revenue Diversification](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/13/supporting-nigeria-homegrown-reforms-new-world-bank-financing-for-inclusive-growth-and-revenue-diversification) — World Bank, June 13, 2024. Claim summary: The Bank approved a $2.25 billion package to support Nigeria’s stabilization effort, revenue reforms, and support for the poor, which is strong external validation of the reform path even as conditions stayed hard. Question IDs: `8B.*`, `8D.*`

- [President Tinubu’s Broadcast on the Nationwide Protest](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/) — State House, August 4, 2024. Claim summary: Tinubu acknowledged violent nationwide protests tied to bad governance and economic hardship, including deaths and destruction, which captures the political cost of the 2024 economic mood. Question IDs: `8C.*`, `8D.*`

- [At least 3 killed in Nigeria at protests over high cost of living](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376) — Reuters via Investing.com, August 1, 2024. Claim summary: Reuters reported nationwide protests against cost of living and governance issues, with at least three protesters killed in Kaduna; the story also recorded Tinubu’s defense that reforms were necessary after years of mismanagement. Question IDs: `8B.*`, `8C.*`, `8D.*`

- [Nigeria: Police used excessive force to violently quash #Endbadgovernance protests](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/) — Amnesty International, November 28, 2024. Claim summary: Amnesty said police used excessive force during the August protests, killing at least 24 people and detaining more than 1,200, which is the clearest rights-cost evidence in the 2024 record. Question IDs: `8C.*`, `8D.*`

- [Staying the Course on Reforms: Progress Amidst Challenges](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/17/nigeria-staying-the-course-on-reforms-progress-amidst-challenges) — World Bank, October 17, 2024. Claim summary: The World Bank said reforms since May 2023 had improved macro stability, fiscal health, and reserves, but also emphasized that households and businesses still faced short-term pain and that inflation remained elevated. Question IDs: `8B.*`, `8D.*`

## Short synthesis

Tinubu’s 2024 term looked like a high-reform, high-distress presidency: international lenders repeatedly credited the administration with serious macroeconomic reforms, while domestic and human-rights sources documented severe hardship, protest waves, security incidents, and harsh police responses.
